column2: The year's return, royal expedition season, Joab and all Israel's dispatch, devastation and siege contrast with David staying in Jerusalem.

column3: It was said renders the unexpressed speaker of said impersonally. Whether David or an unnamed informant supplies the question remains unresolved; Eliam is not substituted for Eliab.

column3: Uriah is the contextual referent supplied for an unexpressed subject, not a separately repeated Greek proper name.

Propose you all shall withdraw for the plural withdrawal verb, distinguishing the collective retreat from the singular initial order to bring Uriah forward. Being struck and dying remain the intended sequence.

column3: The king addresses the messenger but refers to the plural attacking party; ordinary English you carries that contextual plural without changing the cited conduct.

column3: The repetition is part of the selected running text, not treated as an accidental duplicate to remove.

column3: Opening hoti can introduce the report or answer David's why causally; inherited direct reporting remains provisional and does not claim a uniquely settled discourse function.

column3: The final him is distinguished from direct your in the nested message; the instruction is not made another command for Joab to encourage an unnamed person.

column2: Uriah's wife hears that her husband died and beats herself in mourning; repeated marital identification remains.
Mourning passes before David brings her home, she becomes his wife and bears a son; the closing divine judgment explicitly calls David's deed evil.
The Lord sends Nathan, who presents two men in one city, rich and poor; the story's setting is not confused with an identified historical lawsuit.
Very many flocks and herds retain the rich man's abundance in both categories.
Nothing except one little ewe, acquisition, preservation, rearing, shared childhood, bread, cup, bosom and daughter comparison all remain.
The visitor and traveling stranger remain the occasion; the rich man's sparing his own animals leads to taking and preparing the poor man's lamb.
David's intense anger and oath declare the offender deserving death; deserves death renders son of death idiomatically without removing the judgment.
Sevenfold repayment remains the selected number, with both the deed and lack of pity as reasons; fourfold is not substituted.
Nathan's identification and repeated divine I am the One retain anointing and rescue from Saul; God's you remains ordinary human address to David.
The former lord's house and wives in David's bosom, Israel and Judah's house, and possible further gifts remain.
column3: The statement is retained without supplying a historical reconciliation of which wives or households are meant.

column2: Treating the Lord's word as worthless, evil in His eyes, Uriah's death, taking his wife and use of Ammon's sword preserve direct attribution of responsibility to David.
The sword's nondeparture for ever is linked to contempt for God and taking Uriah's wife; no reduced duration is supplied.
Behold introduces God raising calamities from David's own house, taking wives before his eyes and giving them to a neighbour who lies with them before this sun.
Propose For you acted in secret, preserving hoti as the explanatory link to the public action before all Israel and this sun.
David confesses sin against the Lord; Nathan declares the Lord has put it away and emphatically denies David's death, without deleting the following consequence.
The selected object provoked is the Lord's enemies, with emphatic provocation and the child's certain death.
column3: The relation between enemies and provocation is difficult; blasphemed the Lord or caused enemies to blaspheme is not silently substituted.

column2: Nathan departs and the Lord strikes the child borne by Uriah's wife to David, followed by illness.
column3: Struck down is not interpreted as immediate death: the following illness and seventh-day death remain explicit. The force of the crushing verb remains a lexical review question.

column2: David seeks God, fasts and spends the night in sackcloth on the ground; the selected sackcloth is not omitted.
Household elders attempt to raise him, but he refuses and does not share their bread; both refusals remain.
Propose Behold at the servants' opening and He will do harmful things for the future poiesei rather than He may. The seventh-day death, fearful withholding and prior refusal to listen remain.
column3: Will is the servants' feared prediction, not the narrator predicting an actual act; no self-harm mechanism or specific harmful deed is supplied.

column2: Whispering leads David to perceive the death, then ask directly and receive a direct affirmative answer.

The servants recall fasting, weeping and keeping vigil while the child lived, contrasted with rising, eating and drinking after death; the longer selected list remains.
David's prior fasting and weeping express an uncertain hope for divine mercy and the child's life, not a guaranteed promise he expected fulfilled.
The child's death, fasting question, inability to bring him back and David going to him rather than his returning remain without an added afterlife description.
Comforting Bathsheba, intercourse, conception, birth, Solomon's naming and the Lord's love remain.
column3: She named construes the unexpressed naming subject with the preceding conception/birth subject; another subject is grammatically possible and the naming agent remains provisional.

column2: Sending through Nathan and the Idedi naming because of the Lord retain the selected short name.
column3: The sender and naming subject are not explicitly named in this unit; inherited He/he remains open rather than a settled identification of both agents.

David gathers all the people, goes to Rabbah, fights and captures it; no harmonized chronology of partial captures is supplied.
Melchol their king, crown from his head, a talent of gold and precious stone, David's head and abundant spoil remain.
column3: The royal name, crown weight and stone relation are unresolved; Milcom or an imagined wearing mechanism is not silently substituted.
